_source: The Wind Waker save file and the UI that reads it, mined read-only from the zeldaret/tww decompilation at Z:/memRip/sources/tww (GC retail, VERSION > VERSION_DEMO branches). Structure: `_save_layout` is the byte-for-byte content of one save slot -- `blocks` are the top-level members of dSv_save_c in the order the game packs them onto the memory card, each with `mem_offset` (offset inside the in-RAM dSv_save_c, which has alignment padding) and `packed_offset` (offset inside the on-card blob, which does not); `members` lists the fields inside each block with offsets relative to that block. `_persistence` covers checksum/slots/init/reinit. `_menus` is one entry per pause-menu screen with the save fields it reads and whether its code survives decompilation. `_hud` is the same for d_meter.cpp. `_remake_mapping` compares all of the above against the remake's flat-JSON save in gcrip/godot.py. `_unknowns` lists what could not be determined. Every claim carries a `src` of the form path:line that was actually read. `confidence`: high = read straight from the header or decompiled C++; medium = inferred from surrounding code; low = guess. Offsets are hex strings. Cross-references: per-dungeon state (dSv_memBit_c) is fully documented in ww_dungeons.json and only summarised here; the event-bit/event-register encoding is restated once because the save layout is meaningless without it.

_save_layout.packing_note: The in-RAM struct has three alignment holes (0x08E, 0x0C1, 0x37C inside dSv_player_c per include/d/d_save.h:612,616,623, plus 4 bytes at the end of dSv_save_c per :911). dSv_info_c::memory_to_card memcpy's each member back-to-back with no padding (src/d/d_save.cpp:1703-1791), so the on-card image is 0x768 bytes = dSv_save_c::PACKED_STRUCT_SIZE (include/d/d_save.h:899-904). card_to_memory is the exact inverse (src/d/d_save.cpp:1794-1878).
_save_layout.packed_offsets_verified_by: d_file_select.cpp reads the packed blob directly to draw the file-select cards: max life at +0x00 and current life at +0x02 (src/d/d_file_select.cpp:646-648), the Triforce-shard byte at +0xBC and the goddess-pearl byte at +0xBD (src/d/d_file_select.cpp:684,722). Those land exactly on packed mCollect(0xB2)+0xA and +0xB, which independently confirms the whole packed offset table below.

blocks.name: mPlayer.mPlayerStatusA
blocks.purpose: Hearts, magic, rupees, wallet tier, and the item/equip button assignments.

members.name: mMaxLife
members.meaning: Max health in QUARTER-hearts. Fresh file = 12 (3 hearts), src/d/d_save.cpp:26. Clamped to 0x50 = 80 = 20 hearts, src/d/d_meter.cpp:1417. A Piece of Heart adds 1 (src/d/d_item.cpp:584), a Heart Container adds 4 (src/d/d_item.cpp:589). There is NO separate heart-piece counter: the loose-piece count is just mMaxLife % 4, computed on demand (src/d/d_menu_collect.cpp:1647, :3558).

members.name: mLife
members.meaning: Current health in quarter-hearts. Fresh file = 12 (src/d/d_save.cpp:27). On save it is floored to 12 so you can never resume nearly dead: `if (status_a->getLife() < 0xC) status_a->setLife(0xC)` (src/d/d_save.cpp:1710-1712).

members.name: field_0x6

members.name: field_0x8

members.name: mSelectItem
members.meaning: Inventory slot index assigned to each item button. Header comment says 'X, Y, Z button' (include/d/d_save.h:45) but the array is 5 long while dItemBtn_COUNT_e is 3 (include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:1097-1103). Values are dInventorySlot_e indices, 0xFF = none. Init fills all 5 with dItemNo_NONE_e (src/d/d_save.cpp:30-33).

members.name: mSelectEquip
members.meaning: Equipped item NUMBER (not slot) per equip category. Header comment 'Sword, Shield, Bracelet, ?' (include/d/d_save.h:46). 0 = sword (src/d/d_item.cpp:849), 1 = shield (:867), 2 = Power Bracelets (:742). NOTE a real out-of-bounds bug: the recollection code reads and writes mSelectEquip[4], which is actually mWalletSize -- the decomp flags it as a probable bug (src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:1503,1548 and the comment at :1546-1548).

members.name: mWalletSize
members.meaning: Wallet tier. getRupeeMax(): 0 -> 200, 1 -> 1000, 2+ -> 5000 (include/d/d_save.h:20-30). Upgrades set 1 and 2 (src/d/d_item.cpp:1357,1362).

members.name: mMaxMagic
members.meaning: Magic meter capacity. Fresh file = 0 (no meter at all). The Deku Leaf grants 16 (src/d/d_item.cpp:813); the Great-Fairy upgrade grants 32 (src/d/d_item.cpp:1397). Clamped to 0x20 = 32 (src/d/d_meter.cpp:4013-4016).

members.name: (alignment padding)
members.meaning: 1 byte of alignment padding, explicitly labelled in the header (include/d/d_save.h:52). Still written to the card because memory_to_card memcpy's sizeof(class).

members.meaning: Room number. Fresh file = dIsleRoom_OutsetIsland_e = 44 (src/d/d_save.cpp:65). On the sea, room number IS the island index+1; the full island table is dIslandRoomNo_e at include/d/d_save.h:301-354.

members.meaning: OPAQUE, not even zeroed by init. Header names them unk (include/d/d_save.h:95-96).

blocks.cross_reference: This is the FALLBACK only. Where a resuming save actually lands is decided by the l_checkData continue table in dComIfGs_setGameStartStage (src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:1293-1311), which walks event bits RODE_KORL / MET_KORL / UNK_0801 / UNK_0808 / UNK_2401 and falls through to sea room 44 point 128.

blocks.name: mPlayer.mPlayerItem
blocks.purpose: The 21 main inventory slots. mItems[slot] = item number, 0xFF = empty.
blocks.notes: Bottles are slots 14-17 and the VALUE in the slot encodes the contents (empty bottle / red potion / green potion / fairy / forest water / etc). Swapping contents is dSv_player_item_c::setBottleItemIn (src/d/d_save.cpp:86-98). Slots 24-31 / 36-43 / 48-55 are virtual: dComIfGs_getItem routes them to the spoils bag, bait bag and delivery bag respectively (include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:1110-1128).

blocks.name: mPlayer.mGetItem
blocks.purpose: 21 bytes x 8 bits = 'has this item ever been obtained' / per-bottle-content-known flags. Parallel to mPlayerItem: mItemFlags[inventory_slot], bit index 0..7.
blocks.notes: For bottles, onBottleItem() maps each possible bottle content to one bit of mItemFlags[0] (src/d/d_save.cpp:224-283), which is how the item screen knows which contents you have ever held. Distinct from mPlayerItem, which holds what you have RIGHT NOW.

blocks.name: mPlayer.mItemRecord

members.meaning: 'Chart obtained' bits, 128 of them, indexed by chart number (src/d/d_save.cpp:852-861). getCollectMapNum() counts charts 1..61 excluding 35, 36 and anything >= 52 (src/d/d_save.cpp:918-927) -- that count is what the quest screen prints.

members.name: mFmapBits
members.meaning: Per-island bits, one byte per dIslandIndex_e (0..48, include/d/d_save.h:356-408). Bit 0 = 'save-arrived at this grid square' (src/d/d_save.cpp:942-951); bit 1 = the same for the GBA/Tingle link (src/d/d_save.cpp:954-963). A fresh file pre-sets bits 0|1 on Forsaken Fortress, Outset and Windfall (src/d/d_save.cpp:842-844).

members.name: field_0x71
members.meaning: OPAQUE. Zeroed by init (src/d/d_save.cpp:846-848). No accessor found.

members.name: field_0x81

members.name: field_0x82

members.name: field_0x0

members.name: mDeathCount
members.meaning: Deaths, saturating at 9999 (include/d/d_save.h:450-453). Offset inferred from struct layout, not from a header comment.

members.name: mPlayerName

members.name: field_0x25

members.name: field_0x36
members.meaning: Third name copy, same default (src/d/d_save.cpp:977). Purpose unknown.

members.name: mPuzzleData
members.meaning: Entries 0..15 are piece positions written by the puzzle actor d_a_obj_apzl (src/d/d_a_obj_apzl.cpp:443); entry 16 is a separate clear-count exposed as getPuzzleInfo/setPuzzleInfo (include/d/d_save.h:454-455, read at src/d/d_a_obj_apzl.cpp:827,1073).

members.name: mClearCount
members.meaning: Number of times the game has been cleared. Explicitly preserved across a Second Quest reset (src/d/d_save.cpp:1435,1465).

members.name: mRandomSalvagePoint
members.meaning: Randomised 0..2 on a new file (src/d/d_save.cpp:986-989); forced to 3 by the Second Quest reinit (src/d/d_save.cpp:1478).

members.name: field_0x5a

blocks.note: dSv_player_status_c_c::init() is an EMPTY function (src/d/d_save.cpp:1033), so these blocks are never explicitly cleared -- dSv_player_c::init does not even call it (src/d/d_save.cpp:1036-1051). They are whatever the memory held until a boss is first beaten.

blocks.name: mMemory[16]
blocks.purpose: Per-stage persistent state: chests, switches, items, visited rooms, small keys, dungeon items.
blocks.src: include/d/d_save.h:628-683, :719-729, :907; slot enum SaveStageTbl at include/d/d_save.h:879-897
blocks.cross_reference: FULLY DOCUMENTED ALREADY in gcrip/data/ww_dungeons.json -- 32 chest bits (mTbox, src/d/d_save.cpp:1072-1081), 128 switches (mSwitch[4], :1084-1109), 64 item bits (mItem[1] but asserted < 64, :1112-1121), 64 visited-room bits (mVisitedRoom[2], :1124-1133), mKeyNum, and the 6-bit mDungeonItem mask MAP/COMPASS/BOSS_KEY/STAGE_BOSS_ENEMY/STAGE_LIFE/STAGE_BOSS_DEMO (include/d/d_save.h:630-637, src/d/d_save.cpp:1136-1150).
blocks.slot_selection: The slot for the current stage is bits 1..7 of STAG byte 0x09: dStage_stagInfo_GetSaveTbl(i) = (mProp >> 1) & 0x7F (include/d/d_stage.h:1023, mProp at include/d/d_stage.h:70). dSv_info_c::getSave/putSave copy that slot in and out of the live scratch copy dSv_info_c::mMemory (src/d/d_save.cpp:1506-1515).

blocks.name: mOcean
blocks.purpose: 50 x u16 = 800 bits of per-sea-grid state (salvage points looted, etc).
blocks.src: include/d/d_save.h:685-694, init at src/d/d_save.cpp:1157-1161, on/is at :1164-1175
blocks.note: Indexed [grid 0..0x31][bit 0..15], both asserted (src/d/d_save.cpp:1165-1166). The array is declared u16 field_0x0[50] with no descriptive name; 0..0x31 is 50 entries matching the 49 islands plus index 0.

blocks.name: mEvent
blocks.purpose: The 256-byte story-flag array. Event BITS and event REGISTERS share it.
blocks.encoding: For a 16-bit id, the HIGH byte (id >> 8) is the array index and the LOW byte (id & 0xFF) is a MASK, not a bit number. onEventBit: mFlags[id>>8] |= (id & 0xFF) (src/d/d_save.cpp:1188). setEventReg: clears the mask bits then ORs the value in -- mFlags[reg>>8] &= ~(u8)reg; mFlags[reg>>8] |= value (src/d/d_save.cpp:1202-1205). getEventReg returns (u8)reg & mFlags[reg>>8] (src/d/d_save.cpp:1208-1210), i.e. the value is stored UNSHIFTED inside the mask.
blocks.fresh_file: init() zeroes all 256 bytes and then calls setInitEventBit() (src/d/d_save.cpp:1178-1184), which sets exactly two registers: UNK_BEFF = daNpc_Kg1_c::m_highscore and UNK_7EFF = 0xE (src/d/d_save_init.cpp:11-14). Note 0xFF-masked ids are full-byte registers.
blocks.flag_names: The symbolic id list is in include/d/d_save_event_flag.inc, included at include/d/d_save.h:990.

blocks.name: mReserve
blocks.purpose: 80 reserved bytes. Zeroed by init (src/d/d_save.cpp:1213-1217) and copied to/from the card, but nothing else in src/ reads or writes them.

blocks.name: (tail padding)
blocks.purpose: 4 bytes of padding at the end of the in-RAM dSv_save_c only; not part of the packed 0x768 image.

not_saved.note: dSv_info_c is the live game-state object and is much bigger than the saved part. Everything after mSavedata is RAM-only -- memory_to_card never touches it (src/d/d_save.cpp:1703-1791).

members.name: mMemory
members.meaning: Scratch copy of the CURRENT stage's memBit; swapped with mSavedata.mMemory[slot] by getSave/putSave (src/d/d_save.cpp:1506-1515). Saving the game calls dComIfGs_putSave first (src/d/d_menu_save.cpp:935).

members.name: mDan
members.meaning: 64 per-dungeon-visit switches plus a GBA rupee counter, keyed on a stage number that is reset to -1 on leaving (include/d/d_save.h:731-746).

members.name: mZone[32]
members.meaning: Per-zone temporary switches (48), item bits (16) and 512 actor flags (include/d/d_save.h:748-789). Lost on stage change.

members.name: mRestart
members.meaning: Respawn position/room/param for death and room transitions (include/d/d_save.h:791-829).

members.name: mTmp
members.meaning: A SECOND 256-byte event array for temporary flags, same encoding as the saved one. Names in include/d/d_save_event_tmp_flag.inc (include/d/d_save.h:992). Cleared by dSv_info_c::init (src/d/d_save.cpp:1394).

members.name: mTurnRestart
members.meaning: Position/angle plus the King of Red Lions' position/angle and a has-ship flag, for re-entering a stage (include/d/d_save.h:831-862).

members.name: mDataNum
members.meaning: Which of the 3 card slots this session belongs to (src/d/d_file_select.cpp:811, :3725).

members.name: mNewFile
members.meaning: Set to 1 when the slot has never been written (src/d/d_menu_save.cpp:878).

members.name: mNoFile
members.meaning: 'No file present' flag (src/d/d_menu_save.cpp:1057).

members.name: mMemCardCheckID
members.meaning: Card serial number this save belongs to; compared against mDoMemCd_getCardSerialNo() to detect a swapped card (src/d/d_file_select.cpp:3665).

blocks.content: mDoMemCdRWm_HeaderData -- 0xE00 banner, 0xE00 icon, 32-byte comment, 32-byte info string (include/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.h:9-15). Built fresh on every save (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:207-242).

9 x card_pictdata -- 3 pictograph slots per game slot, at (dataNum*3 + 3 + i) (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:85-90). Each is 0x2000: a 0x1EE0 CMPR texture for a 152x104 photo, a photo index, a detail byte, a capture format, and a u16 checksum at +0x1FFE (include/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.h:17-27).

fields.name: save_count
fields.meaning: Incrementing save counter on NTSC (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:51); on PAL the field is reused to hold the language index instead (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:53).

fields.name: gamedata
fields.meaning: THREE save slots, 0x770 each. Each is 0x768 packed save bytes followed by a u64 checksum (include/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.h:29-33).

fields.name: field_0x1658
fields.meaning: Unused filler, memset to 0 before each write (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:46).

two_copy_scheme.write: mDoMemCdRWm_Store writes the header to block 0, then writes the SAME card_savedata to block 1, reads it back and verifies the checksum, then writes it to block 2 and verifies again (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:31-68). The in-game save call is mDoMemCd_Save(ptr, 0x1650, 0) -- 0x1650 = 3 x 0x770, all three slots at once (src/d/d_file_select.cpp:3721).
two_copy_scheme.read: mDoMemCdRWm_Restore reads block 1 and block 2, tests all six per-slot game checksums, and REPAIRS block 1 from block 2 slot by slot where block 1's checksum failed and block 2's passed; if any repair happened it rewrites both blocks (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:124-159). If all six fail the data is marked invalid and pictographs are not loaded (:148-150, :173).
two_copy_scheme.known_bug: The slot-1 repair tests csum2b (block 2 slot 2) instead of csum1b (block 2 slot 1) before copying block 2's slot 1 -- flagged in the decomp as a probable typo (src/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.cpp:138).

checksums.name: game data (per slot)
checksums.algorithm: Byte-wise: c0 += byte, c1 += ~byte over all 0x768 bytes; result is (c0 << 32) | c1. Note c0/c1 are u32 so they do not truncate the way the 16-bit variant does.

checksums.name: card_savedata block
checksums.algorithm: Halfword-wise: c0 += u16, c1 += ~u16 over (0x2000 - 4) bytes; result (c0 << 16) | c1, both halves u16.

init.behaviour: dSv_info_c::init() calls mSavedata.init() (which inits the player block, all 16 memory slots, the ocean bits and the event array -- src/d/d_save.cpp:1494-1503), then clears the scratch memBit, the dan bits, all 32 zones and the temporary event array, and finally resets two static NPC globals (the ship-race rupee count and result).
init.fresh_file_summary: 3 hearts (12 quarter-units) full, 0 rupees, wallet tier 0 (cap 200), no magic meter, every inventory slot 0xFF, all bags empty, no songs/shards/pearls, wind angle -1/-1, time 165.0, day 0, return place = sea room 44 point 206, event array all zero except registers UNK_BEFF and UNK_7EFF.

reinit_second_quest.behaviour: Wipes the file via init() but explicitly carries over: 17 event REGISTERS held in l_holdEventReg (UNK_95FF, 94FF, 93FF, 92FF, 91FF, 90FF, 8FFF, 8EFF, 8DFF, 8CFF, B1FF, 9CFF, 84FF, 83FF, 82FF, 81FF, 80FF -- all 0xFF-masked, i.e. whole-byte counters/records), the clear count, the player name, all four Options settings, the pictograph count, and register UNK_89FF.
reinit_second_quest.then_sets: Five event bits from l_onEventBit (UNK_2F08, UNK_2F04, UNK_2F02, UNK_3A01, UNK_3401), register UNK_C407 = 7, one chest bit (STAGE_MISC #0x00), two sea switches (STAGE_SEA #0x47 and #0x5E), salvage point = 3, and grants the Deluxe Picto Box in the CAMERA slot with both of its get-item bits.
reinit_second_quest.why_it_matters: This is the game's own definition of 'progress worth keeping': a name, the options, the clear count, the picture count, and seventeen 0xFF-masked registers. Everything else -- items, hearts, charts, dungeon state -- is considered disposable.

initdata_to_card.behaviour: Writes a default-constructed save into an empty card slot. Two documented quirks: the player-info block is memset to zero rather than copied from the initialised object (:1959-1962), and a single stack dSv_memory_c is memcpy'd for 16 slots' worth of bytes, so 15 of the 16 stage tables are filled with adjacent stack garbage (:1984-1993). The decomp notes this is harmless because starting a new game re-inits them anyway.

save_flow_in_game.steps: check mNewFile / mNoFile / mMemCardCheckID (:923-927) -> dComIfGs_exchangePlayerRecollectionData (:934) -> dComIfGs_putSave(current stage) to flush the scratch memBit (:935) -> dComIfGs_setGameStartStage to compute the continue point (:936) -> dComIfGs_setMemoryToCard(buf, dataNum) (:1013) -> mDoMemCdRWm_SetCheckSumGameData(buf, dataNum) (:1016) -> card write.

_hud.nonmatching_note: All 16 marked functions still have complete bodies -- in d_meter the marker means the compiled output does not byte-match, not that code is missing. Example: dMeter_magicInitTrans at src/d/d_meter.cpp:4240-4245 is marked 'Nonmatching - regalloc' and is fully readable. There is no inline assembly in the file.
_hud.architecture: Not a class per widget. One god object `sub_meter_class : msg_class` (include/d/d_meter.h:554) holds ~200 fopMsgM_pane_class members, and free functions named dMeter_<element><Init|Move|Draw|Alpha|Trans> operate on it. Entry points dMeter_Create (:7444), dMeter_Execute (:7280), dMeter_Draw (:7183), dMeter_Delete (:7365). Two draw nodes actually blit: dDlst_2DMETER1_c::draw (:1062) and dDlst_2DMETER2_c::draw (:1078). Every pane-name binding is in one place, dMeter_screenDataSet (:6988) -- that is the fastest widget-to-field map.

elements.arithmetic: 4 life units per heart. containers = mMaxHP / 4; partial-heart index = (mCurrHP - 1) / 4; that heart's fill state = mCurrHP % 4 (src/d/d_meter.cpp:1228-1241). Texture by state: 0 -> heart.bti (full), 1/2/3 -> heart_03/02/01.bti (quarter/half/three-quarter), 4 -> heart_04.bti (empty container), 5 -> pane hidden (src/d/d_meter.cpp:1031, :1254). Hard cap 20 panes (:1231, include/d/d_meter.h:576). Max life clamped to 0x50 at :1417.
elements.heart_pieces: No stored counter -- pieces are mMaxLife % 4, only surfaced on the quest screen (src/d/d_menu_collect.cpp:3558). Piece = +1 (src/d/d_item.cpp:584), container = +4 (src/d/d_item.cpp:589).

elements.layout_quirk: The magic bar shifts down 22px when mMaxLife <= 0x2B (43 quarter-hearts = 10 containers + 3 pips), i.e. while the heart row still fits on one line (src/d/d_meter.cpp:4221-4225, same test at :4201, :4243, :4259, :4279).

_remake_mapping._note: The remake's save is a flat Godot Dictionary in gcrip/godot.py (defaults at gcrip/godot.py:3217-3219, reset at :3383-3385). The key list below was taken from the actual code, which carries a few more keys than the brief mentioned.

already_modelled.match: exact -- both are quarter-hearts, both default to 12
exact -- quarter-hearts, default 12, and gcrip/godot.py:2829 iterates hearts_max/4 exactly like dMeter_heartScaleInit
partial -- the remake starts at 16; WW starts at 0 and only grants a meter with the Deku Leaf (src/d/d_item.cpp:813). The remake has no mMaxMagic equivalent.
value matches; no wallet tier, so no 200/1000/5000 cap
conceptual only -- the remake uses a name->bool dictionary (gcrip/godot.py:4419-4426) instead of a 21-slot array of item numbers, so it cannot express bottle contents, bag contents, or slot ordering
exact in meaning; defaults 30/30 (gcrip/godot.py:436-437) match the WW pickup values (src/d/d_item.cpp:737, :796). No mItemMax capacities, so no quiver/bomb-bag upgrades.

EXACT -- the remake stores a raw 256-byte array and reproduces WW's mask semantics faithfully: index = (id >> 8) & 0xFF, test = value & (id & 0xFF), register read = value & (id & 0xFF) (gcrip/godot.py:4434, :4448) mirroring src/d/d_save.cpp:1188-1210
conceptual -- the remake uses its own DAY_UNITS scale (gcrip/godot.py:4202-4220) rather than WW's 165.0-based float, but the pair (day counter + time-of-day float) is the same shape
conceptual -- a flat dictionary (gcrip/godot.py:4679-4685) rather than WW's split between saved per-stage switches, RAM-only per-zone switches and RAM-only dan switches
conceptual -- the remake keys it by name, e.g. "nayru" (gcrip/godot.py:4232), against WW's 3-bit mask (include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:1671-1675)
partial -- one button instead of three, and it stores an item name rather than an inventory slot index (gcrip/godot.py:435)
conceptual -- and note WW does NOT save these; they are RAM-only. WW's saved equivalent is mReturnPlace plus the dComIfGs_setGameStartStage continue table.
